on_tight_canyon.blurb: Tight Canyon is a compact section of Devil's Glen on the Niagara Escarpment in the Beaver Valley, south of Georgian Bay. Much of the climbing sits inside a narrow gully where the walls meet at a right angle, which gives it an enclosed feel. There are about two dozen routes, roughly two thirds bolted and the rest trad. The range is wide: a handful of easy leads in the 5.5 to 5.8 band, a solid middle of 5.9 and 5.10, and a good number of 5.11 and 5.12 lines, plus one 5.13 for the strong. It suits a mixed party where one person wants a gentle warm-up and the other wants to push.

on_kelso.blurb: Kelso is a band of limestone cliff on the Niagara Escarpment near Milton, tucked beneath a ski hill and within easy reach of the Toronto area. The face looks north, so it stays cool and shaded, which helps on hot days. Trad leading dominates, with a smaller group of bolted lines, and the grades lean moderate: a few scrambly or easy pitches, a good cluster from 5.7 to 5.9, then several 5.10s and only a couple of 5.11s. Some lines are multi-pitch, so bring a healthy rack, and expect to build your own anchors on many routes.

on_b_movie_wall.blurb: B-Movie Wall is the busiest face at White Bluff, a sport area on the Bruce Peninsula near Lion's Head, overlooking Georgian Bay. It holds about two dozen bolted routes, nearly all short, roughly 45 to 60 feet, and steep. The grading is hard: a couple of lower routes, then a big block of 5.11 and 5.12, so this is not a place for beginners. Holds are mostly pockets, with some edges and jugs, and the wall has an overhanging, bouldery feel. It catches morning sun and goes into shade later, and tree cover keeps some lines shaded. A dozen quickdraws is plenty.

on_big_boy_wall.blurb: Big Boy Wall is one of the main faces at The Swamp, a newer sport crag in the Kolapore uplands near Collingwood. The wall is a long fin of rock, about 100 metres end to end, and carries some of the best climbing at the crag. Most of the two dozen routes are bolted, with just a few trad lines. Expect hard sport climbing: a few easy lines, a small group of 5.9 to 5.11, and a big share of 5.12 and 5.13. The crag has plenty of tree cover, with sun and shade mixed through the day, and it is reached by a trail with a side path to the base.

on_overhanging_wall_2.blurb: Overhanging Wall is a steep face at Metcalfe Rock, a dolostone cliff in the hills near Collingwood. It carries about two dozen routes, a little over half bolted and the rest trad, with a bias toward difficulty: a few easier leads at the low end, a thin band of 5.9 and 5.10, then plenty of 5.11 and 5.12, and a few 5.13 and harder. The wall can seep, and holds on some lines occasionally break, so grades may feel inconsistent. Metcalfe is mostly shaded under trees and tends to be quiet on weekdays.

on_a_the_turtle.blurb: The Turtle is a limestone sport crag just around the corner from the main Mount Nemo cliffs, close to Milton and about 45 minutes from Toronto. All two dozen or so routes are bolted, and the grades suit climbers moving up from the beginner level: lots of 5.9 to 5.11, with a few easier warm-ups. The climbing ranges from steep, powerful pulling to technical pocket and small-edge work, with sharp crimps and pockets reminiscent of Grassi Lakes. The bolting is solid and the rock is clean, which makes it a fun place for a moderate day out.

on_blank_canvas.blurb: Blank Canvas is a wall at Devil's Glen on the Niagara Escarpment in the Beaver Valley, picking up just to the right of the Into the Shade section. It offers both bolted and trad lines, about two dozen in total, with sport routes making up the majority. Most of the climbing is hard: only a handful of routes sit below 5.9, while a large share fall at 5.11 and 5.12, and a few go into 5.13 and beyond. A pair of well-rated lines in the 5.8 range offer something for moderate climbers. Devil's Glen as a whole is a busy weekend destination.

on_looney_tunes_area.blurb: Looney Tunes Area is a popular section of Devil's Glen, in the Beaver Valley on the Niagara Escarpment, with a healthy mix of trad and sport lines. Around two dozen routes are listed, about two thirds bolted. The grades span a broad range: a few 5.7 and 5.8 lines make good starter leads, a middle group sits at 5.9 and 5.10, and there are several 5.11 and 5.12 routes plus a couple of 5.13s and harder for strong climbers. A few of the classic lines here draw the most attention, so expect company on busy days.
